blocks.text: The Incident of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) in this regard

Hadhrat Naafi says, "Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) used to gather all of his family to eat from one platter every night. It often happened that when he heard the plea of a poor person, he would take his share of meat and bread to the poor person. However, by the time he gave the food away and returned, the others would have finished everything in the platter. If I found anything in the platter, he would also find it, otherwise he would fast in the morning."[^2]
The Incident of a Bedouin with Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ entered the Masjid one day wearing a shawl from Najraan that had thick edging. A Bedouin came from behind and pulled at a corner of the shawl so hard that the edging left marks on Rasulullaah ﷺ's neck. Te Bedouin said, "O Muhammad! Give some of Allaah's money that you have with you!" Rasulullaah ﷺ turned around and smiled. He then said to the Sahabah (RA), "Give him something."[^3]

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "We used to sit with Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid in the mornings and when he stood up to leave, we would also stand and remain standing until he entered his room. On one occasion, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up to leave and had reached the centre of the Masjid when a Bedouin met him and said, "O Muhammad! Give me two camels to ride because you are neither giving them from your own wealth nor from the wealth of your father!" As he met Rasulullaah ﷺ, he pulled so hard on Rasulullaah ﷺ's shawl that it left a red streak across his neck. Rasulullaah ﷺ then thrice repeated, "No. I seek Allaah's forgiveness. Not until you allow me to take retribution (for the injury you have caused me)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then (forgave the man and) and called someone saying, "Give him two camels, one loaded with barley and the other loaded with dates."[^4]
